slot.brief: Write the correct Ksp expression (with powers) for a sparingly soluble salt; test also solubility in common-ion solution.

stem: For the sparingly soluble salt $\text{PbI}_2$, which option gives its $K_{sp}$ expression and the effect on its molar solubility when a small amount of $\text{KI}$ is added?

verdicts.working: PbI₂(s) ⇌ Pb²⁺ + 2I⁻, so Ksp = [Pb²⁺][I⁻]². Added KI supplies the common ion I⁻, decreasing PbI₂ molar solubility.

working:
$\text{PbI}_2(s)\rightleftharpoons\text{Pb}^{2+}+2\text{I}^-$; $K_{sp}=[\text{Pb}^{2+}][\text{I}^-]^2$. Added $\text{I}^-$ shifts dissolution equilibrium left, so solubility decreases.

Independent check: PbI₂(s) ⇌ Pb²⁺ + 2I⁻, so Ksp = [Pb²⁺][I⁻]². Added KI supplies the common ion I⁻, decreasing PbI₂ molar solubility.
